now_the_spec_says: Every summons carries a pickup lifecycle the ticket shows: waiting (no pickup yet), then in-process (picked up, journaled). Stated once at the grammar level, every summons in every class inherits it; terminals take no phase. The ticket is THE SOURCE PERIOD.
context: Ruled 2026-08-07 in design conversation, off the tier-2 close-out. The trigger was CC describing who would flip a hypothetical status marker: the tester picks up the ticket, and suddenly tester, builder, and board each need to know something special about somebody else — the encapsulation smell Akien named stinky. His resolution is structural: the lifecycle lives on the workflow state itself, in the one table (WorkflowDefinition.md), as a property of SUMMONSES AS A KIND — his 'and so on' generalizes past BUILDME to every -ME state, including classes and summonses that do not exist yet (DESIGNME). Settled at approval: the phase is cursor annotation ([BUILDME:waiting] -> [BUILDME:in-process]), not doubled table rows, so the grammar states it once; the rule is 'if the state summons somebody, it has a pickup' — terminals like PROVED take none; the phases map onto the board tri-state exactly (waiting=pending, in-process=in-flight, crossed=done); a pickup is a journaled act (actor + time) through the same one door as every crossing. His VALIDATEME is this file's 2026-08-07 corrected name for the PROVEME summons; the rename does not touch the ruling. WHAT DIES is an idea never built, so no file dies: CC's floated packet-marker (a PENDING field on ruling packets — a per-surface status an actor would have to know to push) is retired by this ruling before it ever reached disk; the board derives waiting/in-flight/done from the ticket's cursor phase, never a side-channel. Per WorkflowDefinition.md's own living-definition rule, the change lands in that file FIRST and everything downstream follows.
